parakeet: The archaeological and historical consequences would be equally decisive. A global flood would require a universal human reset. All civilizations would show sudden collapse at the same time. Writing systems and architectural traditions would restart from zero, and population growth would reflect a sharp, recent bottleneck. Oral traditions across the world would converge on a shared memory of near total extinction. Instead, Egyptian civilization continues uninterrupted through the proposed flood period. Mesopotamian cities show continuity rather than abandonment. Chinese, Indus Valley, and Andean cultures exhibit no synchronized collapse, and human population growth curves show no universal reset. History does not behave like a world that drowned. If Genesis 6 through 9 were literal history, at least one of several conditions would necessarily be true today. All modern humans would descend from a single family only a few thousand years ago, with clear genetic markers reflecting that bottleneck. All land animals would trace back to a single geographic dispersal point with migration patterns matching post flood movement. Earth's geological record would preserve a single recent global catastrophe layer. Every ancient culture would retain memory of total extinction rather than regional flooding. Modern ecosystems would be fragile, simplified, and recently assembled. None of these conditions are met.
